B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Honeycomb announced hosted MCP access for all Honeycomb teams at no additional charge. The team must enable Honeycomb Intelligence.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Free plan: up to 20 million events and 100 million metric data points per month. Pro starts at $150 per month. Enterprise pricing is quote-based.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: MCP is included in the listed Free, Pro, and Enterprise plans; plan event and metric-volume allowances apply to the Honeycomb software.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Honeycomb Intelligence must be enabled for the team. OAuth or a Management API key is required. Team Owners create API keys. Read access is required for operations; writes require mcp:write. get_service_map is Enterprise-only. Tool loading can be narrowed with X-MCP-Toolset: all (default), query, or canvas. API-key rate limits are per key; OAuth limits are shared per user. MCP agent sessions may time out after 24 hours.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Honeycomb controls plan availability, endpoint behavior, and per-tool limits; team owners control team enablement and API-key creation and permissions; users grant OAuth permissions and select client configuration.

The endpoint's 401 points to https://mcp.honeycomb.io/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. The supplied path-suffixed protected-resource document repeats the same resource, authorization server, scopes, and bearer method. Supplied authorization-server metadata: issuer https://ui.honeycomb.io; authorization endpoint https://ui.honeycomb.io/oauth/authorize; token endpoint https://ui.honeycomb.io/oauth/token; introspection endpoint https://ui.honeycomb.io/oauth/introspect; registration endpoint https://ui.honeycomb.io/oauth/register; response_types_supported code; grant_types_supported authorization_code and refresh_token; token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported none, client_secret_basic, client_secret_post; code_challenge_methods_supported S256; introspection_endpoint_auth_methods_supported client_secret_basic and client_secret_post; client_id_metadata_document_supported true. D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official reference labels 25 tools read and 9 write; it does not say whether MCP readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, or openWorldHint annotations are sent. No delete tool appears in the documented list. 2. Write tools require mcp:write; docs describe permissions and OAuth consent, but no per-call confirmation parameter or server-enforced preview/approval flow is documented. 3. OAuth scopes are mcp:read and mcp:write. API keys require read access for all operations and write for mutations, plus environment access; only Team Owners can create keys. Honeycomb Intelligence must be enabled. Team role affects Activity Log Environment exposure: only Team Owners see it through MCP. Redirect-URI approval, token lifetime, and revocation details are not found; troubleshooting says MCP agent sessions may time out after 24 hours. 4. X-MCP-Toolset supports all (default), query, and canvas; it narrows loaded tools/prompts but does not grant access. Unknown or empty values cause requests that include the header to be rejected. US and EU endpoints are documented. No separate read-only endpoint or sandbox endpoint is documented. 5. The docs describe environment permissions and access limits but do not specify MCP-specific PII masking or field redaction. AI terms prohibit processing sensitive personal data and certain heightened-regulation data through Honeycomb Intelligence. 6. Published per-minute limits: 300 for semantic-convention tools and canvas_agent_poll_response; 200 for get_workspace_context, get_dataset, get_environment, list_boards, list_recipients, find_columns, refinery_docs; 150 for get_triggers, get_anomaly_service_profiles, find_queries, get_query_results; 100 for run_query, get_trace, get_dataset_columns, get_slos, feedback; 30 for update_trigger/update_slo; 20 for create_trigger/create_slo/create_recipient/canvas_agent_invoke; 10 for get_service_map; 50 default otherwise. Limits may change. Query docs describe sampling metadata and usage_mode; no general result truncation or call cost is stated. 7. Input schemas, unknown-argument rejection, coercion, parameter correction, and operator overrides are not described for the hosted server. 8. The reviewed MCP docs do not describe MCP request audit records or telemetry collection. The concepts page says the Activity Log Environment is exposed to MCP only for Team Owners; this does not establish what MCP calls are logged. 9. The tool list includes feedback, described as submitting server-experience feedback to Honeycomb; no other feedback, rating, survey, or report tool appears. No documented result upsell. 10. Optional agent skills and setup commands are distributed in honeycombio/agent-skill; they are separate from the server. Server tool descriptions include workflow guidance, but the hosted server's enforcement of those instructions is not documented. 11. No memory feature that changes future outputs or tool availability is documented. 12. US and EU hosted endpoints are documented. Canvas invocation can route to a user's agent in an existing investigation or create a new investigation, then be polled. The docs do not describe this as a proxy hierarchy. 13. The official list contains no raw API request, arbitrary SQL, or script-execution tool.

E_aggregated.token_method: The hosted server's tool definitions and initialize instructions are not publicly available verbatim; the public tool reference provides descriptions but not complete schemas.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The documented MCP tool list contains no telemetry-ingest or instrumentation tool; Honeycomb directs users to separate Send Data with AI workflows for getting data into Honeycomb. No delete tool appears in the official 34-tool list. This compares the published MCP surface, not every UI or REST API operation.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The tool reference says agents call get_workspace_context first and recommends list_boards before update_board. Troubleshooting recommends priming context with team, environment, and dataset information. These are documented agent-use recommendations; public evidence does not show server enforcement.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Honeycomb Intelligence terms state: “Customer grants Honeycomb a worldwide, fully paid-up, royalty-free, and non-exclusive license to use, reproduce, adapt, modify, host, maintain, compile, translate, share and distribute such Input and Output for the purpose of providing Honeycomb Intelligence to Customer, creating and improving Honeycomb Intelligence features, and collecting and using aggregated, anonymized usage and performance statistics”. The terms prohibit use of Honeycomb Intelligence to process sensitive personal data and specified heightened-regulation data, including PHI and GDPR special-category data. Personal-information processing is subject to the applicable DPA and listed subprocessors.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Honeycomb says MCP write tools require mcp:write, which is granted explicitly during OAuth consent or configured on an API key. The toolset header narrows which tools load but does not grant access. The AI terms assign any rights Honeycomb has in Output to the customer.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The write-scope and toolset restrictions are described for the hosted server, but public code for that server is unavailable. Data-use terms are contractual statements; the reviewed MCP docs do not describe MCP-specific masking, retention, or request logging logic. Tool-use recommendations are documentation text, not demonstrated server-enforced rules.

observations_for_research: The hosted service is closed-source, while an archived MIT-licensed self-hosted stdio server exists as a distinct deprecated variant.
The public tool reference exposes descriptions, read/write labels, and rate limits but not input schemas or MCP annotations.
The server supports toolset filtering through a request header; the docs say this affects loading, not authorization.
The official server exposes a feedback submission tool, and its documentation gives a natural-language instruction for using it.
